QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_13

question.text: Which structural feature is PERMITTED for Category III AIFs but NOT typically for Category I or Category II AIFs per SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Charging a management fee in addition to a performance fee
Pooling capital from multiple investors into a single scheme
Accepting capital from FPIs and NRIs
Being structured as an open-ended fund with daily or pre-determined redemption frequency

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Cat III AIFs are uniquely permitted to be open-ended (hedge-fund style) with redemptions at daily/monthly/quarterly frequencies as disclosed in the PPM. Cat I and Cat II are typically close-ended. Section 4.2.3 describes Cat III as including 'funds which are open-ended' — a defining feature. **The Trap:** Options A, B and C are all common features across all AIF categories. Only the open-ended structure is category-distinctive to Cat III. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C (All-Cat) tests this distinction directly. XIX-E as the Cat III Manager exam focuses on operationalising the open-ended structure — daily NAV, subscription/redemption windows, gate clauses, side-pocket triggers. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** An open-ended Cat III fund needs DAILY NAV infrastructure, cut-off times (typically 3 PM IST), gate clauses (e.g., 10% of NAV per month), and a notice period (30-90 days) for large redemptions. If your illiquid exposure breaches the normal liquidity profile, use a side-pocket to protect remaining LPs from forced sales.
